source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS Astronomical-Book fragments (4Q208-4Q211; late 3rd c. BCE through late 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Ge'ez (medieval; only complete witness, heavy abridgment of the Aramaic original) as fallback. NO continuous Greek witness for chs 72-82.
source.transliteration_convention: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic per Milik 1976 + Tigchelaar-García Martínez DJD XXXVI 2000 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Ge'ez SBL convention.
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976, Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000, Drawnel 2011, Neugebauer 1985.
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 + Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI + Drawnel 2011 Aramaic Astronomical Book + Black 1985 + Charles 1912 + Knibb 1978 + Nickelsburg-VanderKam 2012.
source.citation: Milik 1976; Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; Drawnel 2011; Black 1985 (with Neugebauer 1985); Charles 1912 PD; Knibb 1978; Nickelsburg-VanderKam 2012; VanderKam 1998 Calendars in the DSS.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 74 — THE MOON'S IRREGULAR CYCLE: 354-day lunar year vs 364-day solar year (the 10-day gap), plus the larger 3-year synchronism. **The 4Q209 fragments here are denser than the Ge'ez** — 4Q209 frags 7-25 preserve substantial parallel material for chs 74-79, with calendrical computations on lunar-vs-solar reconciliation that the Ge'ez abbreviates.

verses.text_geez: ወካዕበ፡ ሑረታ፡ ካልዕተ፡ አርአየኒ፡ ለወርኅ፡ ወሕገገ፡ ሑረቶሙ፡ ኵሎ፡ ሕገገ፡ ለበበ፡ ወርኅ፡
verses.translit: wa-kāʿba ḥuratā kāləʿta ʾarʾayanī la-warḫ wa-ḥəgaga ḥuratomu kwəlo ḥəgaga laba-warḫ
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 col. iii preserves partial parallel (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000)
verses.notes: Uriel shows another course of the moon and its monthly laws.

verses.text_geez: ወኵሉ፡ ሕገጊሆሙ፡ አርአየኒ፡ ኦሪኤል፡ መልአክ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ዘሀሎ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወከመ፡ ይከውን፡ ለቀዋምቶሙ፡ ስማቲሆሙ፡ ጸሐፍኩ፡
verses.translit: wa-kwəlu ḥəgagihomu ʾarʾayanī ʾUrʾēl malʾak qəddus zahallo məslēya wa-kama yəkawwən la-qawāmtomu səmātihomu ṣaḥafku
verses.notes: **Enoch records the names of the lunar positions.** The Enoch-as-celestial-scribe motif (cf. 1 En 33:4; cf. 3 Enoch / Metatron tradition).

verses.text_geez: ወጸሐፈ፡ ሊተ፡ መንበሮሙ፡ ዘበበ፡ ወርኆሙ፡ ወዘበበ፡ ብርሃኖሙ፡ እስከ፡ ይትፌጸም፡ በበ፡ ዐሥር፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ ዕለታት፡
verses.translit: wa-ṣaḥafa lita manbaromu zababa warḫomu wa-zababa bərhānomu ʾəska yətfēṣam baba ʿaśr wa-ʾarbāʿtu ʿəlatāt
verses.notes: **14-day completion of the waxing cycle.** Records of lunar position and luminosity per the 14-day waxing.

verses.text_geez: በስብዐቱ፡ ቀዳምያን፡ መንበራት፡ ለብርሃና፡ ምሉአ፡ ብርሃና፡ ይከውን፡ በበ፡ ስብዕ፡ ምክፋላት፡
verses.translit: ba-səbʿatu qadāməyān manbarāt la-bərhānā məluʾa bərhānā yəkawwən baba səbʿ məkəfālāt
verses.notes: Seven 'first stations' for the moon at sevenths-of-full-light. This is the discrete-quantization of lunar luminosity into a 7×7 = 49-unit visible-light grid (4Q208 preserves this scheme more clearly than the Ge'ez).

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብኡ፡ ኪያሁ፡ ስብዐቱ፡ መንበራት፡ ዘስብዐቱ፡ ምክፋላት፡ ለብርሃና፡ በምዕራባት፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾu kiyāhu səbʿatu manbarāt zasəbʿatu məkəfālāt la-bərhānā ba-məʿrābāt
verses.notes: Western mirror-stations of the waning moon — symmetric inverse of the eastern waxing-stations.

verses.text_geez: ወእለሰ፡ ቀዋምት፡ ዘይትፈለጡ፡ ላዕለ፡ ኩሎሙ፡ ሕገጊሆሙ፡ በበ፡ ወርኆሙ፡ ወበበ፡ ዓመቶሙ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾəlasa qawāmt zayətfaḷaṭu lāʿla kwəlomu ḥəgagihomu baba warḫomu wa-baba ʿāmatomu
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic not preserved at this verse
verses.notes: Stations distinguished by month and year.

verses.text_geez: ወያመጽእ፡ ወይትገብእ፡ ለፀሐይ፡ ቀዳማዊ፡ መንበር፡ በአንቀጽ፡ ዘይትፈለጥ፡ ሰማንየ፡ ዕለታት፡
verses.translit: wa-yāmaṣṣəʾ wa-yətgabbəʾ la-ḍaḥay qadāmāwi manbar ba-ʾanqaḍ zayətfaḷaṭ samānya ʿəlatāt
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 col. iii fragmentary (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000)
verses.notes: Solar-lunar synchronism via a gate-distance computation; difficult Ge'ez.

verses.text_geez: ወአናቅጽ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ፀሐይ፡ የሐውር፡ በውስቴቶሙ፡ ለሠላሳ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ምስለ፡ መራኅት፡ ለበበ፡ ጊዜሁ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾanāqəḍ ʾəmənnehomu yəwaḍḍəʾ ḍaḥay yaḥawwər ba-wəstētomu la-śallāsā mawāʿəla məsla marāḫət laba-gizēhu
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic not preserved at this verse
verses.notes: Restatement of 72:6 — sun in each gate 30 days. Used here as anchor for lunar-solar comparison.

verses.text_geez: ወአናቅጽ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ ወርኅ፡ ስድስቱ፡ መንገል፡ ይከውን፡ ሙያው፡ ለወርኅ፡ ወእምነ፡ መንገሊሆሙ፡ ካዕበ፡ ይትገብእ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾanāqəḍ ʾəmənnehomu yəwaḍḍəʾ warḫ sədəstu mangal yəkawwən muyāw la-warḫ wa-ʾəmənna mangalihomu kāʿba yətgabbəʾ
verses.witness_primary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 8 preserves partial parallel: 'six gates' for the moon (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000)
verses.text_aramaic: ותרעיא די מנהון יפק שהרא שתא תרעין הוין מהלכה לשהרא ומן מהלכיהון תוב יתוב
verses.notes: **The moon also uses the 6-gate system** (east 1-6) — same eastern gates as the sun, but the moon's traversal-rate is different (because the synodic month ≠ solar month). 4Q209 preserves the moon-gate notice in Aramaic.

verses.text_geez: ወእም፡ ሐመሰ፡ ምክፋላተ፡ ዕለታት፡ ዓመተ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ይትፌጸም፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ ስድሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾəm-ḥammasa məkəfālāta ʿəlatāt ʿāmata ḍaḥay yətfēṣam śallastu məʾət sədsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl
verses.notes: **364-day solar year confirmed at this junction.**

verses.text_geez: ወይትኄፀጹ፡ ዓመተ፡ ወርኅ፡ ዐሠርተ፡ መዋዕለ፡ እምነ፡ ዓመተ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወይከውን፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ ሐምሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡
verses.translit: wa-yətḫēḍaṣu ʿāmata warḫ ʿaśarta mawāʿəla ʾəmənna ʿāmata ḍaḥay wa-yəkawwən śallastu məʾət ḥamsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl
verses.witness_primary: Aramaic 4Q209 frag 7 col. iii preserves trace of '354 days' lunar-year (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 145-148; Drawnel 2011 pp. 252-260)
verses.text_aramaic: ויחסר שנת סיהרא עשרה יומין מן שנת שמשא ויהוה תלת מאה חמשין וארבעה יומין
verses.notes: **THE 10-DAY LUNAR-SOLAR GAP: lunar year 354 days, solar year 364 days; gap = 10 days.** This is the calendrical-DIAGNOSTIC verse of the Astronomical Book — establishes the ratio basis for the rest of the chapter's reconciliation computations. **CROSS-CORPUS**: Mesopotamian astronomy calculated the lunar-solar gap as ~10.875 days (the basis of the 19-year Metonic cycle); the Astronomical Book schematizes this to exactly 10 days. Cf. Jubilees 6:36-38 (polemic against the lunar year). **The Qumran 364-day calendar's calendrical-superiority claim** depends on this gap analysis.

verses.text_geez: ወይትገብኡ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወከዋክብት፡ ለማእክለ፡ ኵሉ፡ ዓመታት፡ ምስለ፡ መንበሮሙ፡ ቅዱም፡ ወይትኀደጉ፡ ዘበጊዜሆሙ፡ አርባዕተ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ዘኢተሐስቡ፡ በኆለቅ፡ ለዓመት፡
verses.translit: wa-yətgabbəʾu ḍaḥay wa-kawākəbt la-māʾəkla kwəlu ʿāmatāt məsla manbaromu qəddum wa-yətḫaddagu zababa gizēhomu ʾarbāʿta mawāʿəla zaʾitaḥasabu ba-ḫolaq la-ʿāmat
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic not preserved at this verse
verses.notes: **THE FOUR EPACT-DAYS 'NOT COUNTED' IN THE [LUNAR] RECKONING.** The polemic-edge: those who use the 354-day lunar count are explicitly missing 4 days at the year-junctures + 10 days from the lunar-vs-solar gap. **PROLEPSIS OF 1 EN 82:5-6** — the explicit polemic. Editor will need to handle this as the central calendrical-identity claim of the Qumran community.

verses.text_geez: ወአርባዕተ፡ ዓመተ፡ ይትፌጸም፡ አሐደ፡ ሺህ፡ ወአርባዕተ፡ ምእተ፡ ሰብዐ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ዓመተ፡ ፀሐይ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾarbāʿta ʿāmata yətfēṣam ʾaḥada śiḥ wa-ʾarbāʿta məʾəta sabʿa mawāʿəla ʿāmata ḍaḥay
verses.witness_primary: Ge'ez (Charles 1912 74:13; Knibb 1978 vol. 2 p. 171); Aramaic 4Q209 frag 9 may preserve fragmentary '1,460 days' computation (Drawnel 2011)
verses.notes: **4-year solar cycle = 1,456 days (= 4 × 364). The Ge'ez reads 1,470 (an error?) — likely textual corruption.** Charles 1912 conjectured emendation to 1,456. The 4Q209 Aramaic stratum likely preserved the correct figure. Editor will need to handle the manuscript-traditional uncertainty.

verses.text_geez: ወአርባዕተ፡ ዓመተ፡ ለወርኅ፡ ይትፌጸም፡ አሐደ፡ ሺህ፡ ወምእተ፡ ስድሳ፡ ወሰላሳ፡ ወክልኤተ፡ መዋዕለ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾarbāʿta ʿāmata la-warḫ yətfēṣam ʾaḥada śiḥ wa-məʾəta sədsā wa-salāsā wa-kəlʾēta mawāʿəla
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q209 fragments preserve trace lunar-year multi-year totals (Drawnel 2011)
verses.notes: **4-year LUNAR total = 1,416 days (= 4 × 354). Ge'ez reads 1,432 — likely corrupted.** Charles 1912 emendation: 1,416. The lunar 4-year is 40 days short of the solar 4-year (40 = 4 × 10, confirming the 10-day annual gap).

verses.text_geez: ወይትፌጸም፡ ቅያስ፡ በውስተ፡ ሣልስ፡ ዓመት፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ ስድሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ወእምነ፡ ወርኅ፡ ይትኄፀጽ፡ ሰላሳ፡ መዋዕል፡
verses.translit: wa-yətfēṣam qəyās ba-wəsta śāləs ʿāmat śallastu məʾət sədsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl wa-ʾəmənna warḫ yətḫēḍaṣ salāsā mawāʿəl
verses.notes: **THE 3-YEAR INTERCALATION: by year 3, the lunar count is 30 days short of the solar, so an intercalary month (30 days) reconciles them.** This is the 3-year-intercalation mechanism — a SCHEMATIC version of the Babylonian 8-year + Greek 19-year (Metonic) intercalation. Editor: this is the practical-calendar-management content.

verses.text_geez: ወይከውን፡ በሣልስ፡ ዓመት፡ ሠለስቱ፡ ምእት፡ ሰላሳ፡ ወአርባዕቱ፡ መዋዕል፡
verses.translit: wa-yəkawwən ba-śāləs ʿāmat śallastu məʾət salāsā wa-ʾarbāʿtu mawāʿəl
verses.notes: Third-year cumulative lunar total: 1,062 days (= 3 × 354). The figure here in the Ge'ez is again corrupted; reads '334' which Charles 1912 emends.

verses.text_geez: ወይትኄፀጽ፡ ዓመተ፡ ወርኅ፡ እምነ፡ ዓመተ፡ ፀሐይ፡ ወከዋክብት፡ ናኦቶ፡ ሰላሳ፡ መዋዕል፡
verses.translit: wa-yətḫēḍaṣ ʿāmata warḫ ʾəmənna ʿāmata ḍaḥay wa-kawākəbt nāʾoto salāsā mawāʿəl
verses.notes: Closing summary: 3-year lunar-vs-solar deficit = 30 days (3 × 10). The 30-day shortfall is exactly the intercalary-month length, so the system self-corrects every 3 years. **The Astronomical Book's schematic intercalation = a 1/3-year average of 10 days/year converted to lump-sum every 3 years.**
